DESCRIPTION: Darolutamide (Standard) is the analytical standard of Darolutamide (HY-16985). This product is intended for research and analytical applications. Darolutamide (ODM-201) is an orally active competitive androgen receptor (AR) antagonist, with a Ki of 11 nM for rat wild-type AR (wtAR) and an IC50 of 26 nM for human wild-type AR (hAR)-mediated transcriptional activation[1]. Darolutamide inhibits testosterone-induced AR nuclear translocation and transcriptional activation[1]. Darolutamide exerts selective effects on AR-positive cells by inhibiting AR-dependent signaling pathways, and its active metabolite retains full antagonistic activity against AR mutants[1]. Darolutamide can be used for the research of prostate cancer, including androgen receptor-dependent prostate cancer[1].

  •  Process development and optimization
  •  Manufacturing and scale-up
  •  Fully equipped analytical facilities for validation
  •  GMP synthesis of lipid components

- Extensive Sample Extraction Experience

- Experience with Nearly 50 Types of Matrix

- Metabolite Identification

- Integrated Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in clinical trials

DESCRIPTION: Naltrexone is an opiate sold under the trade names Revia, Depade and Vivitrol® and is prescribed primarily for the management of alcohol or opiate dependence. This analytical reference standard is applicable for use in LC/MS or GC/MS applications such as pharmaceutical research, forensic analysis, clinical toxicology, pain prescription monitoring or urine drug testing. Naltrexone research solution: Research utilizes naltrexone in thermosensitive gels to enhance microneedle-assisted transdermal delivery, showcasing its potential for non-invasive therapeutic applications and improving drug bioavailability (Polymers (Basel), 2021; doi: 10.3390/polym13060933). Opioid receptor antagonist: A study discusses the historical context of opioid use disorder trials, with naltrexone featured as a pivotal medication in optimizing treatment strategies. This research underscores its importance in addiction studies and the development of effective treatment modalities (Addict Sci Clin Pract, 2021; doi: 10.1186/s13722-021-00223-z). Naltrexone in vitro study: The compound is utilized in a model of ocular neuropathic pain, highlighting its utility in pain management research and its potential role in developing new therapeutic strategies for chronic pain conditions (Transl Vis Sci Technol, 2019; doi: 10.1167/tvst.8.2.6). Naltrexone pharmacological research: Research on Mg²? influx modulation in cardiac myocytes provides insights into ionic exchanges in heart tissues, demonstrating naltrexone?s broader applications in physiological and pharmacological studies (J Physiol Sci, 2019; doi: 10.1007/s12576-018-0625-5). Naltrexone biochemistry application: A study explores mechanical stimulation for reducing ethanol self-administration in rats, indicating naltrexone?s utility in experimental models of addiction and its potential application in behavioral sciences (Evid Based Complement Alternat Med, 2017; doi: 10.1155/2017/6578621).

DESCRIPTION:
Advanced Quantitative LNP Characterization

(characterization of statistically sparse sub-populations or for critical applications (i.e. to support IND filings)


Application:

The characterization package is designed to deliver rapid and statistically robust numerical results that describe critical LNP morphology parameters of a physical LNP sample. The increased statistical robustness of this characterization package enables an evaluation of subtle differences in otherwise homogeneous LNP sample cohorts. The maximal reliability of the numerical data and the formal report documents that are delivered with every analysis are well perceived by authorities to demonstrate the quality of the presented LNP product (i.e. during IND filings or process changes).

 

5000 individual LNPs are characterized per sample to minimize sampling error and ensure reliable, statistically relevant numerical results. Intermediate precision studies demonstrate a Standard Deviation of < 1.0 nm for the average particle diameter and < 1.5% Standard deviation for LNP morphology classification between independently repeated measurements of the same sample.

Due to the high accuracy and precision, the results provide a significant quantitative understanding of the morphology and composition of the analyzed LNP material and are typically used to track and detect intricate changes in LNP size and morphology during formulation optimization, upscaling or stability testing. Furthermore, Advanced Quantitative Characterization package provides a statistically robust numerical report on LNP morphology for IND filings or similar quality control/demonstration applications.

 

Package Scope:

·  Cryo-EM Sample preparation on ATEM LNPCfoil grids

·  Cryo-EM Data Collection

·  Validated ATEM AI Data Evaluation

·  Report generation

 

Characterization & Quantification of:

·  Particle Size Distribution

·  Particle Morphology Classification (Solid Core, Biphasic Split, Biphasic Dense (“Blebbed”))

·  Particle Aspect Ratio

 

Deliverables:

· Collection of 5.000 particles (LNP images) or min. 250 cryo-EM micrographs (whichever achieved first)

· PDF Report for each analyzed sample

· Statistical Quantitative Report in Excel Format

 

Additional cryo-EM images are available upon request
